newsitem.title: USA: Judge freezes Calif. man's assets after SEC suit.
newsitem.headline: Judge freezes Calif. man's assets after SEC suit.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Tuesday a Federal judge agreed to freeze a California investment adviser's business assets after the agency sued him for allegedly bilking his clients out of millions of dollars.

The agency said it received the preliminary injunction Tuesday after suing Emmanuel Lagpacan of Layfayette, Calif., on August 1 on allegations he fraudulently offered and sold about $4.4 million in "phony securities" to 73 of his clients.

"Of the more than $4.4 million Lagpacan raised through this scheme, he still owes least $3.1 million of this amount to approximately 50 investors located in California and five other states," the SEC said in its complaint.
Lagpacon, without admitting any wrongdoing agreed to the asset freeze.
In its complaint, the SEC said Lagpacan used the investor proceeds to buy real estate even though he told the investors their funds would be placed in low-risk, government-insured investments.
In recent months, Lagpacan has begun selling the properties purchased with investor funds and "distributing the proceeds unfairly to a small number of favored clients," the agency said.
"More than 40 other clients have received no payments," the SEC said. "Lagpacan has also been lying to clients to cover his earlier fraudulent acts."
Lagpacan's attorney said Lagpacan and the others named in the SEC's suit deny the agency's allegations.
